subject: Cloud Computing
title: Carbon-Aware Computing
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Carbon-Aware Computing.

hook.text: What if your workload ran when electricity was cleanest? Carbon-aware computing schedules by grid emissions.

buildup.text: The carbon intensity of electricity varies by time and location. Midnight wind power is cleaner than noon coal power.

discovery.text: Google already shifts workloads to data centers with the cleanest energy. It's called carbon-intelligent computing.

twist.text: Most workloads can shift by minutes or hours without users noticing. Batch jobs, backups, and training can wait.

climax.text: The Green Software Foundation is standardizing carbon-aware APIs. Any developer can build carbon-aware apps soon.

punchline.text: Run your code when the grid is greenest. Timing matters.

quiz.question: How does carbon-aware computing reduce emissions?
options: By scheduling workloads to run when and where electricity has the lowest carbon intensity
By turning off all data centers during peak hours
By using only solar-powered devices for cloud computing

details.summary: Carbon-aware computing schedules workloads to run when and where the electrical grid is cleanest. By shifting batch jobs to times of high renewable energy availability or to regions with cleaner power, organizations can significantly reduce the carbon footprint of their cloud operations.
details.whyItMatters: Carbon-aware computing reduces emissions without sacrificing performance for latency-sensitive workloads. It leverages the cloud's flexibility to make environmentally better choices automatically.
takeaways: Workloads shift to times when renewable energy is most available
Region selection can reduce carbon by choosing cleaner grids
The Green Software Foundation promotes carbon-aware practices

faq.question: How does carbon-aware scheduling work?
faq.answer: APIs from services like WattTime and Electricity Maps provide real-time carbon intensity data for power grids. Schedulers use this data to delay flexible workloads until carbon intensity drops, or route them to regions with cleaner power at that moment.

faq.question: Which workloads can be carbon-aware?
faq.answer: Batch processing, CI/CD pipelines, ML training, backup jobs, and report generation can be shifted in time. Cross-region workloads can be routed to cleaner regions. Latency-sensitive user-facing applications cannot easily shift but benefit from running in permanently clean regions.
